newsitem.title: UK: Eurobourses end down, rattled by Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Eurobourses end down, rattled by Wall Street.

text.p: European bourses ended sharply down on Wednesday as Wall Street retreated further only a day after U.S. stocks tumbled to their biggest loss in five months.

On currency markets, the dollar regained some poise after a choppy performance ended its rally to a 23-month peak against the mark on Tuesday. Sterling weakened amid fears that its recent strength could harm British industry.
The losses on European bourses ended a record-breaking pace on much of the continent this week fuelled by investors who saw the recent strength of the dollar as a boon to exporters.
London and Paris shares ended showing losses as Wall Street fell 0.4 precent, a follow-on from the wave of profit-taking on Tuesday which wiped 1.21 percent off the Dow Jones industrial average.
Frankfurt finished with a loss of 0.72 percent after hitting a record close of 2,886.98 points on Tuesday.

European bourses were depressed by Tuesday's big fall on Wall Street. Computer-driven sell programs in New York kicked in during a frantic last 10 minutes of trading to lock in profits after the Dow rose 500 points, or eight percent, in November.
"We haven't been following Wall Street up...we have been following it down...but I don't think it will be a disaster by any means," said a dealer in London.
But the gloom in London, where stocks fell 0.44 percent, was slightly offset by the the weaker pound which was seen as helping the exporting sector.
"Sterling is an important factor. If it weakens, it will help a lot of major stocks. So there are other things at work here besides Wall Street," the dealer said.

French stocks suffered the biggest knock from Wall Street, ending down 1.7 percent after a strong performance this week. All CAC-40 stocks closed with losses, apart from Eurotunnel which advanced as the channel tunnel was reopened.
Lagardere fell seven percent to 145 francs, hit hard by suspension of the Thomson privatisation and ensuing uncertainty.
Frankfurt closed down 0.7 percent, sapped by Wall Street's fall and the weaker dollar, after a day of quiet trading. "It's consolidation today," said one traderin Frankfurt.
The dollar's slide hit exporting chemical and auto stocks. BMW, Hoechst and BASF were all lower after surging on Tuesday.
The dollar clawed back some losses against the mark in late European business and traders said sentiment about the dollar remained upbeat despite falling from 23-month peaks on Tuesday.

"The dollar looks quite well poised to go higher. The Germans don't mind it higher, the French want it a lot higher -- everybody seems to be happy with a stronger dollar," said Peter Wood, forex dealer at Bank of Boston in London.

The dollar was quoted at 1.5630 marks in late trade, back near Tuesday's closing levels and well clear of the intraday low of 1.5553 hit when figures showed stronger-than-expected growth in the German economy.

"The market is justified in taking a bearish view of the mark in the absence of any Bundesbank or official German policy challenge to France on the question of the "weak euro'", said Tony Norfield, treasury economist at ABN AMRO here.

French officials have called for a stronger dollar, eager to see the franc weaken against the U.S. currency to help stimulate growth, yet keen that the French currency should not fall against the mark and upset the monetary union process.
Sterling had a rough day, falling to to $1.6408 from $1.6520 late on Tuesday.

The pound's slide from four-year highs started on Tuesday when Finance Minister Kenneth Clarke said industry was starting to fret about the pound's exchange rate. Businessmen are worried that sterling's rally might damage British competitiveness by making exports more expensive.
CURRENCIES
The dollar was quoted at 113.14 yen and 1.5630 marks in late trade against 113.68 yen and 1.5647 marks on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING PRICES
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares ended 16.3 points lower at 4,045.2.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished down 40.46 at 2,308.65.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed down 20.91 at 2,866.07. In post-bourse
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed stronger at $369.95 an ounce, compared to the close on Tuesday of $$367.85. Silver ended at $4.82, up 11 cents.
